scope: Observed agentless recommendation identity and Deployment attribution for one namespace, one Deployment, one container and two ready replicas; no generalized replica-to-finding rule.

findingsObserved.severityVersusRisk: ARG metadata severity is Medium for root filesystem and High for trusted registries; contextual risk.level is Low for both. The portal Risk level column is a different field from metadata severity.
findingsObserved.identityInterpretation: ResourceType remains k8s-container. The identity segment labeled pod- contains the Deployment name; the actual pod name appears in additionalData.podName. The record names topLevelKind Deployment and topLevelName kspm-scope-proof-v2.

addonEvidence.interpretation: AKS configuration did not enumerate an Azure Policy add-on, and Defender reported its add-on recommendation Unhealthy while both KSPM-Agentless findings were present. This demonstrates those two agentless checks in this lab without the add-on; it does not change prerequisites for all workload-hardening checks.

timing.controlPlaneServiceFirstEvaluations: Five cluster-level records report first evaluations during 2026-10-08T05:32:27Z; exact dates are preserved per capture.
timing.collectionGap: No successful exports in this local evidence between approximately 02:09 and 13:20 UTC. Service timestamps are not measured delivery latency or a fixed scan interval.
timing.run1Comparison: Run 1 workload existed about 65 minutes. Its empty captures are consistent with this later run taking about 6.5 hours to first evaluate, but the cause of its empty result is not established.

podReplacement.interpretation: The single-pod replacement was Kubernetes-verified. Before proceeding to the template fix, neither surface supplied independently fresh evidence for that stage. Later template-stage evidence cannot retrospectively prove standalone pod-replacement stability.

portalCorroboration.limitation: Portal row visibility corroborates the recommendations. Exact controller JSON paths are evidenced by ARM and ARG, not claimed legible in the narrow portal grid.

provenance.method: Each source JSON was verified against its SHA-256 sidecar before selecting an explicit field allowlist. Hashes identify the retained source bytes; they do not independently authenticate Azure as origin.
omitted: literal pod names; stable aliases retained
provenance.sourceRecordDescription: Public excerpt is derived from private captures; credential redactions, when present in source captures, are recorded there.

notEstablished: standalone finding stability after single-pod replacement
finding stability through fresh evaluation after template change

templateRemediation.controlInterpretation: Registry/image configuration was unchanged. A fresh trusted-registry record naming a post-rollout pod could corroborate processing of the rolled-out workload; it would not alone establish fresh root-filesystem evaluation or clearance.
templateRemediation.latestServiceResult: Both findings remain Unhealthy, with the pre-intervention pod name and unchanged first-evaluation/status-change dates. These returned payloads do not represent verified post-rollout evaluations.

recordRole: Historical October 8 baseline and intervention excerpts; latest result is run2-post-rollout-evidence.json.

redactionRevision.change: Literal pod names replaced with stable aliases; original source captures, their hashes, observation times and measured outcomes are unchanged. The old deadline is explicitly historical.

aliasScheme.baseline-pod-A: The old pod named by both recommendations before intervention; later deleted during the single-pod phase.
aliasScheme.post-rollout-pod-A: The pod created by the template rollout and named by the refreshed registry finding.
aliasScheme.post-rollout-pod-B: The other pod created by the template rollout.
aliasScheme.single-replacement-pod: Replacement from the inconclusive single-pod phase.
